A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SECA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices through Appendix O are readable and matchable, including the relocated model-version table and newly added checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMLU attack experiments, hallucination and prompt analyses, and comparisons between automated evaluators and human annotators.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the additional GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 now evaluates adversarial strength before feasibility checking and admits proposals improving on the global x_best, rather than checking feasibility first and comparing against each parent prompt x. The underlying proposer, checker, and candidate-search framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same open-ended multiple-choice answering task across the same 16 MMLU subjects. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Raw prompts and GCG remain the attack comparators, with unchanged comparator membership in Table 2. Table 3 retains both human annotators, and Appendix D retains the same illustrative jailbreak methods.

E3.justification: V1 describes a 347-sample dataset and specifies a 218-sample exception only for GCG. V2 Appendix L states that both GCG and SECA use 218-sample subsets during their comparison. This revises the reported sampling setting without establishing reruns. Metric formulas and the coherence threshold of 60 remain unchanged despite SEE/SCE renaming.

E4.justification: The convergence, hallucination-type, lexical-diversity, prompt-length, and evaluator-agreement analyses are retained. Appendices B and K contain the same attack examples; no ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: V1 specifies 10,000 bootstrap samples for standard deviations in Table 2 and Figure 4. V2 checklist item 7 additionally states that all reported means use this resampling. This extends statistical-method disclosure without establishing additional runs or new significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and 8–13 retain their numerical entries, and Figures 3–4 retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports SECA and GCG ASR@30 values of 80.29 and 6.26 for Llama-3-3B in both versions. The sampling-description revision does not accompany changed scores.

T1.justification: V1 Equation (5) imposes PPL(x) <= gamma; v2 Equations (5)–(6) instead require membership in the proposer-generated set X_P and assume those outputs are coherent. This substantively changes the central feasible-set definition and coherence assumption. Equations (1)–(2) also switch from maximization to minimization. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the constrained, gradient-free attack contribution, MCQA effectiveness claims, and findings about linguistic variation. Replacing constraint-violation terminology with semantic-error terminology does not establish a different core empirical claim.

C2.justification: New footnotes explain the lightweight proposer's cost versus hallucination-risk tradeoff and why selective checking permits a stronger, more expensive checker. Section 3.1 adds a rationale for tolerating some incoherence in human-generated prompts. Appendix O's limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that the existing repository includes the experimental dataset, detailed instructions, and usage guidelines. It also identifies the annotators as volunteers familiar with the setup. Prompt templates, model snapshots, hardware, and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The research bibliography and positioning against gibberish, trivial, and meaning-shift attacks remain unchanged. Section 4 and Appendix E retain the same substantive discussion of prior research.

P1.justification: V2 adds a NeurIPS checklist, rewrites portions of the formulation and algorithm explanation, standardizes probability/error terminology, and corrects Appendix M's reference from Figure 4 to Figure 3. The main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 and the regenerated Figure 3 adopt SEE/SCE labels; Table 4 adds their abbreviations. Figure 4b's caption clarifies target-token conditioning. Table widths are adjusted, and Table 7 moves onto a separate page with its caption above it. Existing result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the algorithm, comparison sampling, and reproducibility information, and aligns the coherence formulation more closely with proposer-based generation. However, Equation (2) now minimizes a loss described in Section 2.1 as target-response probability, while Equation (6) maximizes that probability. These documentation gains coexist with an unresolved inconsistency in the central formulation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
